entities.text: Smt. Maitri Rai @ Maitri Devi @ Smt. ... vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Heard the parties.
It is specific case of the petitioner as argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that 1.06 acres of land has already been acquired by the management of CCL and is being used by the CCL.
It has further been argued that though the land has been acquired but till date no compensation has been paid to the petitioner neither employment as per the rules and policies has been provided.

Learned counsel further argues that additionally CCL has acquired 5.78 acres of the land but from the counter affidavit of the State, it appears that land in question i.e., 5.78 acres of the petitioner was never acquired.

Respondent-CCL as well respondent-State is directed to file respective affidavits as to (i) if CCL acquired the land of 1.06 acres which is used as the Railway side why not till date compensation has been paid under new Act to the petitioner who is an old lady aged about 90 years.
(ii) If the land admeasuring 5.78 acres has not been acquired by CCL as per the affidavit of the State why not a notification under form-VI be issued that the same land has not been acquired.
Let respective affidavits to that effect be filed within a period of four weeks.

Put up this case on 13.12.2023."
2.

Learned counsel for the respondent-State and respondent- CCL fairly admits the position that 1.06 acres of land of this petitioner was acquired by CCL, however, the bone of contention remains with regard to payment of compensation, inasmuch as, the respondent-CCL submits that the amount of compensation for 1.06 acres of land has already been paid to the respondent-State along with bulk payment with regard to acquisition of land including of this petitioner.

3. The respondent-State does not dispute the same but this Court feels that due to the internal procedure and mechanism of CCL and the respondent-State, the petitioner who is an old lady shall not suffer for the same.

Accordingly, this Court directs the respondent no.1-Additional Chief Secretary, Revenue Registration and Land Reforms and the General Manager, Land and Revenue,
CCL should sit together in the early next week but not beyond Wednesday i.e. 11.12.2024 and do the needful so that the petitioner shall get the legitimate amount in accordance with the land acquisition scheme.

4. List this case on 16.12.2024.
5.

It goes without saying that on the next date of hearing, i.e on 16.12.2024, either the concerned respondent shall bring the cheque/D.D in favour of the petitioner or any proof of such payment with respect to compensation.
